message.content:
In Christian theology, **Jesus Christ** is regarded as the most important prophetic figure. While the Old Testament contains many revered prophets—such as Moses, Isaiah, Jeremiah, and Daniel—Christians believe that Jesus fulfills and surpasses all of them in several key ways:

| Aspect | Old‑Testament Prophets | Jesus Christ |
|--------|------------------------|--------------|
| **Role** | Foretold God’s covenant, called Israel to repentance, foretold the coming Messiah | Himself is the promised Messiah; He embodies the covenant and brings it to completion |
| **Nature** | Human messengers of God | Divine Son of God, fully human and fully divine |
| **Message** | Calls to faith, justice, and covenant fidelity | Offers salvation, new covenant, and the promise of eternal life |
| **Fulfillment** | Their prophecies point toward the Messiah | He is the fulfillment of those prophecies (e.g., Isaiah 53, Micah 5:2) |

Because of this unique status, Jesus is often called the “Prophet, Priest, and King” in Christian tradition. While other prophets are highly respected and foundational to Christian belief, Jesus is considered the culmination of prophetic revelation and the central figure around whom Christian faith is built.
